scientific_question: Can the Step-14 local Pauli-frame transformation be inferred without revealing the true affected qubit or injection boundary, using only the known reference circuit plus hardware-executable finite-shot Born calibration probes and the model-visible finite-shot diagnostic bundle?

candidate_set.qubits: all logical qubits in the known reference circuit
candidate_set.boundaries: all unique boundaries immediately before or after any CX/CZ event, clipped to 1..len(circuit)-1
candidate_set.filter: candidate qubit must participate in at least one operation before and at least one operation after the boundary

hardware_facing_frame_calibration.probe_strength_source: reuse frozen Step-14 model-blind identifiability probe strength
hardware_facing_frame_calibration.hardware_interpretation: Each candidate response template is estimated from finite-shot plus/minus rotation probe circuits that a future QPU could execute; this simulator diagnostic does not itself validate physical hardware or probe-budget practicality.

deterministic_inference.candidate_mechanism_score: profile Gaussian log-likelihood in shot-whitened evidence space after analytically fitting one signed scalar amplitude to one candidate-axis response
deterministic_inference.primary_pool: uniform-prior log-mean-exp marginalization over candidate locations
deterministic_inference.secondary_pool: maximum profile likelihood over candidate locations

latent_mil_probe.purpose: test whether mechanism labels alone can learn to select/marginalize candidate canonical frames without location supervision
latent_mil_probe.candidate_feature: 24-d canonical feature from each finite-shot candidate frame
latent_mil_probe.pool: masked log-mean-exp over candidates independently for each mechanism logit
